headline: Public docs teardown: highest-impact fixes and the automation layer to prioritize first

summary.executive_summary: Meilisearch documentation spans 1,247 crawled pages with 100% crawl coverage and strong overall retrieval readiness (78.61/100, moderate band). Critical gaps include 16 confirmed broken internal links, API reference coverage at only 61.9% despite 746 API pages detected, and freshness metadata visible on just 31.92% of pages. Evidence backing for claims is moderate at 56.66% (1,323 of 2,335 key claims), and 50.09% of content carries stale risk flags. High confidence in findings (91.5% overall) supports immediate action on link integrity, API documentation completeness, and freshness transparency.

key_findings.headline: Undocumented API operations
key_findings.business_consequence: Generate/update reference + how-to from OpenAPI and enforce drift checks.

key_findings.headline: Documentation freshness debt
key_findings.business_consequence: Prioritize stale pages via weekly SLA loop and lifecycle policies.

key_findings.headline: Code/docs contract drift
key_findings.business_consequence: Track interface changes and enforce docs updates with report-first governance.

priority_actions.title: Fix all 16 confirmed broken internal docs links
priority_actions.why_this_first: Immediate trust and SEO win with minimal engineering effort, directly improves AI citation quality and user navigation across 1,247 pages.

priority_actions.title: Add last-updated timestamps to the 68.08% of pages missing freshness metadata (approximately 849 pages)
priority_actions.why_this_first: Surfaces recency to users and search engines, mitigates 50.09% stale risk perception, and boosts trust with low ongoing maintenance once automated.

priority_actions.title: Close the 38.1% API documentation gap by auditing the 746 detected API pages and adding missing usage examples or cross-links
priority_actions.why_this_first: Developer onboarding and retention hinge on complete API docs; closing this gap reduces support load and accelerates time-to-value for new users.

strengths: Complete crawl coverage at 100% (1,247 of 1,247 pages) with high crawl confidence (95%)
Strong answerability at 97.27% and perfect citationability at 100%, enabling reliable AI-assisted support
High actionability coverage at 80%, indicating clear next-step guidance for users
risks: 16 confirmed broken internal docs links degrade user trust, SEO authority, and AI retrieval quality
API reference coverage at 61.9% leaves 38.1% of API surface undocumented or poorly linked, risking developer churn
Only 31.92% of pages display last-updated metadata, obscuring content freshness and eroding user confidence in accuracy
50.09% stale risk rate indicates half the corpus may appear outdated to users and search engines
limitations: External audit cannot verify runtime correctness of 746 API examples or whether code samples execute successfully against current Meilisearch versions.
Stale risk and freshness scores reflect metadata and heuristics, not actual content accuracy or alignment with the latest Meilisearch release features.
API coverage detection relies on page structure patterns; the 61.9% figure may undercount if reference pages lack standard formatting or are dynamically generated.
automation_first: Deploy a CI link checker to catch the 16 broken internal docs links and prevent future regressions across 1,247 pages, reducing manual QA cycles and preserving SEO equity with zero ongoing effort.

Automate last-updated timestamp injection from Git commit history to cover the 849 pages (68.08%) missing freshness metadata, eliminating manual date maintenance and immediately addressing the 50.09% stale risk perception.
Implement API reference coverage monitoring to track the 746 API pages and alert when new endpoints lack usage docs, preventing the 38.1% gap from widening and reducing developer support escalations.
